task.title: every member verification chain runs miter audit --paths, which requires a repo-local index that nothing creates

events.description: OBSERVED 2026-11-07: verifying CO-8 ran the chain `miter contracts && outfeed lockfiles && miter audit --path . --paths && chalkline docs check --workspace` against `common`, which failed with "miter: no index at common/.gaugeblock/miter/miter.redb: run `miter index <PATH> --db ...` first". Every member chain begins that way, so a member repository cannot pass its own chain from a clean checkout. Related to GB-288 (a member `miter index` writes to the suite root unless --db is passed), which is why the index is never where the chain looks for it.

OBSERVED 2026-11-07: verifying CO-8 ran the chain `miter contracts && outfeed lockfiles && miter audit --path . --paths && chalkline docs check --workspace` against `common`, which failed with "miter: no index at common/.gaugeblock/miter/miter.redb: run `miter index <PATH> --db ...` first". Every member chain begins that way, so a member repository cannot pass its own chain from a clean checkout. Related to GB-288 (a member `miter index` writes to the suite root unless --db is passed), which is why the index is never where the chain looks for it.

CORRECTION 2026-11-07, empirical, run inside common/:

  miter contracts          -> FAILS: no index at common/.gaugeblock/miter/miter.redb
  miter audit --paths      -> PASSES (audit never touches an index; it reads sources and manifests)
  outfeed lockfiles        -> PASSES while printing "All 0 repositories track a fresh Cargo.lock"

So the original title blamed the wrong command. Three facts replace it:

1. MEMBER CHAINS ARE NOT AFFECTED. storypole's chain is fmt + clippy + nextest + `miter audit --paths` + docs check, and it runs clean (SP-33 verified against it). The failure I saw was the HARNESS chain running inside a member repo, which was the chain-fallback bug fixed in a626638. Filing it as a member-chain blocker was reading a symptom of that bug.

2. THE HARNESS CHAIN DOES DEPEND ON AN INDEX NOBODY CREATES. `miter contracts` (the first command of the gaugeblock/default chain) needs an index at the repository it runs in, so the chain cannot pass from a fresh clone until someone runs `miter index`. This is real and will bite CI.

3. `outfeed lockfiles` REPORTS SUCCESS ON AN EMPTY SET. Run inside a member repository it finds zero repositories and says so with exit 0 - the same silence this suite keeps removing. Filed separately.

The fix for (2) should follow GB-237's precedent for reads: a command that needs the index should build it when it is absent rather than instructing the caller to, because an instruction inside a verification chain is a step nobody notices is missing.
